glosses: An inspection or examination.

examples.text: I don't know if she will be there, but it's worth a check.

glosses: A control; a limit or stop.

examples.text: checks and balances
The castle moat should hold the enemy in check.
a remarkable check to the first progress of Christianity

glosses: A situation in which the king is directly threatened by an opposing piece.
A mark (especially a checkmark: ✓) used as an indicator.

examples.text: Norton had made a neat, lawyerly check beside each of the items he and Billy had picked up—half a dozen or so, including the milk and a six-pack of Coke.

glosses: An order to a bank to pay money to a named person or entity.

examples.text: I was not carrying cash, so I wrote a check for the amount.

glosses: A bill, particularly in a restaurant.

examples.text: I summoned the waiter, paid the check, and hurried to leave.

glosses: A maneuver performed by a player to take another player out of the play.

examples.text: The hockey player gave a good hard check to obtain the puck.
Liverpool had been reduced to 10 men in the 88th minute, Ibrahima Konaté collecting a second yellow card for a check on Kai Havertz.

glosses: A token used instead of cash in gaming machines, or in gambling generally.

examples.text: […]the statute prohibits a machine which dispenses checks or tokens for replay[…]

glosses: A lengthwise separation through the growth rings in wood.
A mark, certificate, or token by which errors may be prevented, or a thing or person may be identified.

examples.text: a check given for baggage
a return check on a railroad

glosses: The forsaking by a hawk of its proper game to follow other birds.
A small chink or crack.
To inspect; to examine.

examples.text: Check the oil in your car once a month.
Check whether this page has a watermark.

glosses: To verify the accuracy of a text or translation, usually making some corrections (proofread) or many (copyedit).

To mark items on a list (with a checkmark or by crossing them out) that have been chosen for keeping or removal or that have been dealt with (for example, completed or verified as correct or satisfactory).

examples.text: Check the items on the list that interest you.
Check the correct answer to each question.

glosses: To control, limit, or halt.

examples.text: Check your enthusiasm during a negotiation.

c. 1775–1780, Edmund Burke, letter to the Sheriffs of Bristol
so many clogs to check and retard the headlong course of violence and oppression
She was about to retort but something checked the words on her tongue.

glosses: To scold or rebuke someone.
To verify or compare with a source of information.

examples.text: Check your data against known values.

glosses: To leave in safekeeping.

examples.text: Check your hat and coat at the door.

glosses: To leave with a shipping agent for shipping.

examples.text: Check your bags at the ticket counter before the flight.

glosses: To pass or bounce the ball to an opponent from behind the three-point line and have the opponent pass or bounce it back to start play.

examples.text: He checked the ball and then proceeded to perform a perfect layup.
That basket doesn't count—you forgot to check!

glosses: To disrupt another player with the stick or body to obtain possession of the ball or puck.

examples.text: The hockey player checked the defenceman to obtain the puck.

glosses: To announce that one is remaining in a hand without betting.

examples.text: Tom didn't think he could win, so he checked.

glosses: To make a move which puts an adversary's king in check; to put in check.

examples.text: After I checked my opponent with a pawn, he resigned immediately.

glosses: To chide, rebuke, or reprove.

examples.text: The good king, his master, will check him for it.

glosses: To slack or ease off, as a brace which is too stiffly extended.
To crack or gape open, as wood in drying; or to crack in small checks, as varnish, paint, etc.
To make checks or chinks in; to cause to crack.

examples.text: The sun checks timber.

glosses: To make a stop; to pause.

examples.text: The mind, once jaded by an attempt above its power, either is disabled for the future, or else checks at any vigorous undertaking ever after.

glosses: To clash or interfere.

examples.text: For if it [Loue] checke once with businesse, it troubleth Mens fortunes.

glosses: To act as a curb or restraint.

examples.text: It [his presence] checks too strong upon me.

glosses: To turn, when in pursuit of proper game, and fly after other birds.

examples.text:
And like the haggard, check at every feather
 That comes before his eye.

glosses: To check out, make sense or prove to be the case after verification or interrogation.

examples.text: Didn’t remember that at all. But it sure checks!

glosses: An expression showing that a requirement has been satisfied.

examples.text: Keys? Check. Batteries? Check. We are all ready to go!

glosses: An expression that indicates that the speaker wishes to pay the bill (e.g. in a restaurant).
A pattern made up of a grid of squares of alternating colors; a checkered pattern.

examples.text: The tablecloth had red and white checks.
